# Organisation and Reporting
These policies cover reporting lines, titles and laboratory access for research staff.
## Reporting Lines - Research staff report to the [bold]Lead Researcher[/bold], who runs the laboratory, sets research priorities and signs off on results. - The Lead Researcher reports to the senior Company employee on site. This is normally the Corporate Liaison, unless an employee of grade WYC7 or above is present. - Management may ask about research and is to be answered. Staff may not volunteer details of projects management hasn't asked about. - If the Lead Researcher is absent or incapacitated, the most senior researcher present runs the laboratory until they return.
## Titles Research staff hold academic titles instead of office grades: - [bold]Assistant Professor[/bold] (Assist-Prof.): qualified researcher. All research staff start here. - [bold]Associate Professor[/bold] (Asso-Prof.): experienced researcher. May lead a line of research and supervise others. - [bold]Professor[/bold] (Prof.): held by the Lead Researcher.
Promotion is by time in post and the quality of recorded results.
## Laboratory Access - Research areas are open only to research staff, Corporate Security and the senior employee on site. - Other staff, including office staff, may not be brought into the laboratory. - Requests for access are to be refused and reported to the Lead Researcher.
## Other Departments - [bold]Corporate Security[/bold] protects the laboratory and handles anything dangerous that leaves it. Its instructions are to be followed during an incident. - [bold]Office staff[/bold] handle the site's accounts and freight. They are not cleared for research information. - [bold]Colonial staff[/bold] are not Company employees and may not be told about research under any circumstances.
